title: Paula Modersohn-Becker's birth chart
metaDescription: Paula Modersohn-Becker's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 19.1° Aquarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Tightest of all, Venus holds a sextile to Pluto at 0.3° — close enough to weld taste to depth. A sextile is an offer rather than a given: available when it is reached for, quiet when it is not.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At the noon reference the Sun sits 19.1° into Aquarius — the second decan, which the old scheme hands to Mercury. Same sign, different decan, different chart.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Mercury at 28.6° Aquarius, Venus at 22.0° Pisces, Mars at 16.3° Aries. Mercury in a air sign reads as thought that travels by comparison; Venus in a water sign reads as attraction that works by atmosphere; Mars in a fire sign reads as effort spent in bursts and openings.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Venus and Pluto hold the closest angle here — a sextile, 0.3° wide. The scheme reads a sextile as a door left unlocked. Useful, and entirely dependent on someone walking through it. Behind it, Mercury conjunction Saturn at 1.2°, and Mercury square Jupiter at 1.2° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: The Sun opposes Uranus while both square Pluto. Two squares braced against one opposition make a t-square — the chart’s working end, where pressure keeps finding the same outlet. The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The oldest layer of the scheme — seven planets, four conditions — flags four placements in this chart. The Sun in Aquarius at 19.1° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Venus in Pisces at 22.0° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Mars in Aries at 16.3° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Saturn in Aquarius at 27.4° is in domicile. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Of the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: 3 in air, 2 in water, 2 in fire, 2 in earth by element, 7 fixed, 1 mutable, 1 cardinal by modality. Mercury and Uranus were retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Cancer into Leo during that day at the birthplace, travelling 14.7° between one midnight and the next. A birth time would settle it in a second; there isn’t one. So the Moon stays unnamed here — the alternative is a guess wearing the clothes of a fact.
